purpose: A bounded method for keeping an already-won commercial cleaning contract both profitable and kept: measuring the realized monthly spread per contract against what the bid assumed, decomposing erosion into crew cost drift, scope creep and complaint load, running the acknowledge-correct-verify-close loop that actually retains clients, watching term and notice windows, building and holding honest repricing conversations, expanding healthy accounts into added frequency, periodic services and sister sites, and deciding when a contract must be rescoped, re-crewed, repriced or exited - without ever misrepresenting who cleans the building and without resolving obligation-class questions that belong to a qualified professional.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors

the unit of management is one live recurring monthly commercial cleaning contract at one site, already won under the bid method and delivered by contracted crews the broker arranged; the broker's income is the spread that survives between what the client is invoiced and what the month actually cost to deliver, so every unit here is judged by whether it protects that spread and keeps the client

no price, crew rate, spread percentage, escalation figure, complaint rate, response time, retention rate or account multiple in this knowledge base is a market rate or an industry benchmark; each is a MECHANISM the broker measures inside its own ledger, complaint log and contracts, and re-measures per account

worker classification, insurance, bonding, licensing, non-solicitation, indemnity and termination questions are named only as obligation CLASSES; they vary by jurisdiction, facility type, client and year, must be verified with a qualified professional and the current authority before anything is promised or acted on, and are never carried over from another contract by assumption

the client knows, throughout the life of the account and not only at signing, that cleaning is performed by contracted crews the broker arranges, supervises and stands behind; no retention, repricing or expansion move here depends on the client misunderstanding the service model

clients differ enormously in sophistication inside the same book - a volunteer church administrator, a sole-practitioner dentist, a strata board treasurer and a regional facilities department read a renewal clause differently - so the duty to explain notice windows, escalators and scope changes in plain language scales with that gap
margin is created at bid time and can only be defended afterwards; this method can detect, correct, reprice, re-crew or exit a bad contract, but it cannot retroactively make an under-priced bid whole
this knowledge base is educational business-process knowledge; it is not personalized legal, tax, insurance, employment or financial advice for any particular broker, contract, crew or jurisdiction
exclusions: targeting facility classes and their buying process, walkthrough-based scoping of a prospect, labor-load and production-rate math for a new bid, proposal construction, contract-term drafting and honest differentiation in the pitch: owned by the contract acquisition and bid strategy knowledge base, whose outputs this one inherits as the baseline it measures against

sourcing, vetting and engaging crews or subcontractors, the engagement-structure decision itself, the crew-facing scope-of-work handoff pack, inspection and walkthrough cadence design, quality scoring methodology, supplies and equipment responsibility models, and backup coverage design for crew failure: owned by the crew sourcing, quality control and walkthroughs knowledge base, whose inspection scores and crew records this one consumes as inputs rather than designs

any statement of what a cleaning contract is worth, what a crew is paid, what a healthy spread looks like, how fast a complaint is normally answered, what churn rate is typical, or what a cleaning book sells for, presented as a figure of fact rather than as a mechanism the broker measures in its own accounts

legal conclusions about worker classification, insurance adequacy, bonding, non-solicitation clauses, indemnity allocation, auto-renew or termination enforceability, or facility compliance duties for any particular account or jurisdiction; these are flagged for verification by a qualified professional, never resolved here

retention and repricing tactics that trade on a client's fear, distress, forgetfulness or confusion: health-scare and inspection-failure framing, invented liability threats, silent reliance on a missed auto-renew window, buried escalators, threatened service degradation, access or key leverage, and pressure on an unsophisticated signer to extend a term they do not understand
performing the cleaning itself: chemical selection, equipment operation, floor-care technique, infection-control procedure and any operational instruction to a cleaner

residential and consumer recurring cleaning, one-off consumer jobs, and franchise-system purchase or resale decisions, which carry different buyers, economics and obligation classes than the commercial contracts managed here

competency_questions.question: What margin did this contract actually produce last month, as opposed to the margin the bid assumed it would produce?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CONTRACT_LEDGER_AND_COST_CAPTURE names every delivered-cost line recorded against the site and month and MARGIN_HEALTH_READ turns the gap between bid model and realized spread into a band with a named dominant mechanism

competency_questions.question: Delivered cost at this site has risen since the bid - which mechanism moved it, and does that mechanism point at the crew, the scope, or my own pricing?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CREW_COST_DRIFT_MECHANISM separates rate renegotiation, hours creep, added bodies, coverage premiums, turnover retraining, consumption drift and rework, and assigns each its own remedy path

competency_questions.question: How do I catch work that has been added to this contract without being billed, and what do I do with each addition once I find it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SCOPE_CREEP_LEDGER logs each addition with date, requester and estimated added crew time, and SCOPE_CHANGE_ORDER_DISCIPLINE converts it into a change order, a traded task, or a recorded goodwill item with an expiry - never silent absorption

competency_questions.question: A client just complained - what happens in the first hour, at the next service, and before the item is allowed to close?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COMPLAINT_INTAKE_AND_TRIAGE states the capture channels, severity classes and acknowledgement clock, and COMPLAINT_RESPONSE_LOOP requires acknowledge, correct, verify and written closure with the correction cost posted to the ledger

competency_questions.question: Is this complaint a crew failure, a task that was never in the contract, or a client whose expectations moved - and therefore who pays to fix it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COMPLAINT_ROOT_CAUSE_CLASSIFICATION assigns the complaint to one named cause class and routes execution and coverage failures to free correction while routing scope gaps and expectation drift to a commercial conversation

competency_questions.question: Which of my accounts is most likely to cancel in the next few months, and what signal told me first?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COMPLAINT_LOAD_AS_MARGIN_SIGNAL supplies the normalized complaint trend and re-open share, CLIENT_RELATIONSHIP_MAP supplies the relationship state, and ACCOUNT_HEALTH_SCORECARD combines them with margin band and runway into a ranked action queue

competency_questions.question: The facility manager who hired me has left and a stranger now runs the account - what do I do, and when?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CLIENT_RELATIONSHIP_MAP names the dangerous transitions and the re-onboarding first move, and SERVICE_REVIEW_CADENCE brings the evidence-based review forward so the successor judges the account on a record rather than one bad night

competency_questions.question: When does this contract's renewal, notice or escalator window open, and what must already be done before it does?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RENEWAL_CALENDAR_AND_TERM_WATCH holds term end, auto-renew trigger, notice period, escalator anniversary and certificate expiries with lead-time alarms, and states that clause interpretation is an obligation class routed to a qualified professional

competency_questions.question: How do I build and run a price-increase conversation that survives a rebid threat without fear-selling or ambushing the client?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REPRICING_CASE_CONSTRUCTION assembles dated cost drivers, logged scope additions and the service record into costed options, REPRICING_CONVERSATION sets timing, audience, honest framing and a pre-set walk-away, and ETHICAL_RETENTION_BOUNDARY names the levers that are refused

competency_questions.question: Where is the next recurring dollar inside an account I already hold, and when is it honest and safe to ask for it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ACCOUNT_EXPANSION_MAP lays out the frequency, periodic-service, day-porter, adjacent-area and sister-site ladder and sequences it by demonstrated performance and crew capacity, with SERVICE_REVIEW_CADENCE supplying the proof and the occasion

competency_questions.question: This contract has been under water for months - do I fix it, reprice it or exit it, and how do I exit without harming the client, the crew or my referral base?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: UNPROFITABLE_CONTRACT_EXIT states the remedy ladder that must be exhausted first, the exit triggers, and the exit duties covering notice, client-first communication, transition, crew notice and access return, with abandonment explicitly refused

competency_questions.question: What must this client always be able to say correctly about who cleans their building, and which retention moves am I not allowed to use even when they would work?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HONEST_BROKER_ACCOUNT_COMMUNICATION requires the current contact to know contracted crews perform the work and requires crew changes to be disclosed, and ETHICAL_RETENTION_BOUNDARY enumerates the refused levers and the positive disclosure duties around notice windows and escalators

competency_questions.question: Which facts arising during the life of an account are obligation-class questions I must route to a professional rather than decide myself?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CLASSIFICATION_AND_COMPLIANCE_WATCH lists the live-account triggers - drift toward control over a crew, expiring certificates or endorsements, new site compliance overlays, contested clauses - and produces a dated flag register with referral status instead of an in-house ruling

competency_questions.question: Across the whole book, which accounts deserve investment, which are structurally dangerous, and when should I stop selling?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PORTFOLIO_MARGIN_MIX_AND_CAPACITY reads spread distribution, client and crew concentration, route density and supervisory capacity, and LOSS_AND_SAVE_POST_MORTEM feeds back what actually killed or saved accounts

glossary.definition: What the contract actually left the broker in a given month: the invoiced amount minus every delivered cost recorded against that site and month - crew payment, extra visits, redo and callback labor, broker-supplied consumables, equipment cost, the broker's own site and admin hours, and any credit given. It is a measured quantity per contract-month, never the margin the bid modeled.

The set of mechanisms by which the cost of delivering an unchanged scope rises after signature: a crew renegotiating its rate, real hours exceeding the modeled hours, extra bodies added to hold a shrinking cleaning window, premiums paid for coverage, turnover retraining running below pace, consumable consumption growth, and rework forced by inspection findings.

The unbilled expansion of what the crew does at a site - extra areas, extra frequency, event and post-construction cleanups, 'while you're here' tasks agreed directly with the cleaner, and periodic work drifting from a billed project into an expectation. Creep is a cost mechanism that is invisible until it is logged in hours.

The trend, not the event: complaints per site normalized for size, service frequency and fixture density, tracked for direction, concentration by area or task, share that re-open after closure, and share arriving from above the day-to-day contact. It is read as a leading indicator of both cancellation and margin erosion.

The single named category a complaint is assigned to before any correction is dispatched - scope gap, spec ambiguity, execution failure, coverage failure, supplies or equipment failure, expectation drift, or client-side cause - because the class, not the symptom, decides the remedy and who bears the cost.

The written instrument that converts an agreed change into three simultaneous updates: the client's price and invoice, the crew's scope document and pay, and the site's cost model in the ledger, stated with an effective date and the name of the client-side approver who has authority.

The period before a contract's term end or auto-renew trigger during which either party must give notice to change or end the arrangement. The broker tracks it to act early and discloses it to the client plainly; what a particular clause requires and whether it is enforceable is an obligation-class question for a qualified professional in that jurisdiction.

A contract term providing for a price adjustment at a stated interval or on a stated trigger, such as an anniversary or an index. It is a mechanism whose existence, trigger and calculation must be read from the signed contract of the account in question and explained to the client before it fires, never applied silently.

Project services billed outside the recurring nightly or weekly scope - floor stripping and refinishing, burnishing, carpet extraction, interior window cleaning, high dusting, pressure washing, post-construction cleanups - whose timing lands unevenly across months and therefore distorts any single-month margin read until it is smoothed across the term.

The per-contract state produced by combining the margin band with complaint trend, relationship state and contract runway - for example profitable but relationally fragile, unprofitable but well liked, or unprofitable and already unhappy - because the pair of readings, not either alone, determines whether the next move is a visit, a change order, a repricing case, an expansion offer or an exit.

nodes.definition: Fix what a live contract is accountable for before measuring anything. A signed cleaning contract is not income; it is a monthly promise to deliver a scope at a cost below the invoice, and the broker is paid only by the spread that survives each month. This frame names the unit of management as one contract-month at one site, states which costs count as delivered cost (crew payment, extra or emergency visits, redo labor, consumables the contract puts on the broker, equipment, the broker's own inspection, travel and complaint-handling hours, and any credit issued), and separates three outcomes that a naive 'is the client happy?' view collapses into one: profitable and secure, profitable but at risk of cancelling, and retained but under water. It also fixes what post-signature work can and cannot do - price was set at bid time and delivery capability was set when the crew was engaged, so this book of work can detect, correct, rescope, reprice, re-crew or exit, but it cannot retroactively repair an under-priced bid. Every unit downstream reports into this frame, which is why an account is never judged by the size of its invoice or by the warmth of its last phone call.

included: the contract-month at one site as the unit of management
the list of cost lines that count as delivered cost
the three-way split between profitable-secure, profitable-at-risk and retained-under-water
what post-signature work can and cannot change
excluded: constructing the original bid or its labor-load math, owned by the acquisition knowledge base
designing the crew engagement structure, owned by the crew sourcing knowledge base
any assertion of what a spread should be

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the broker's delivered-cost components change - supplies or equipment moving onto the broker, periodic work brought in-house, or a new contract type entering the book

pros.claim: Naming the contract-month as the unit stops the broker from managing the book by invoice size and reveals which large account is quietly the most expensive to hold
pros.example: the biggest monthly invoice in the book turning out to consume the most unpaid callback trips and broker drive time, while a small twice-weekly office runs untouched

cons.claim: A strictly per-contract frame under-weights effects that only exist at book level, so an isolated read can recommend an exit that damages the wider book
cons.example: dropping a thin-margin site that was the anchor keeping a reliable crew fed inside one territory, after which the neighbouring accounts lose their crew too

failure_modes: treating gross monthly billings as income and never computing what a month cost to deliver
assuming the margin modeled in the bid is the margin being delivered
blaming the crew for what was actually a pricing or scoping failure made before they arrived
acceptance_tests: for every live contract the broker can state the unit (site and month), the full list of delivered-cost lines being captured, and which of the three health outcomes the account currently sits in
revisit_triggers: the broker takes on a contract whose cost structure differs from the rest of the book, for example one where supplies or equipment move onto the broker
a crew engagement structure changes in a way that changes which cost lines the broker bears

nodes.definition: Disclosure is a standing condition of the account, not a sentence said once during the sale. The client was told before signing that cleaning is performed by contracted crews the broker arranges, supervises and stands behind, and every month afterwards must stay consistent with that: when the client asks who is in the building at night, the answer is direct; when a crew is replaced, the client is told before they discover it themselves; when a new contact inherits the account, the model is restated to them because they heard none of the original conversation; and when the broker answers a complaint it promises what it can actually do - dispatch, re-clean, escalate to the crew's principal, replace the crew - without implying an employment relationship it does not have. The unit also governs the small operational honesty that clients notice: who holds keys, alarm codes, badges and access cards, whose insurance certificate is on file, and whose name is on the invoice versus whose people are on the floor. It exists because the moment of exposure is guaranteed - a client eventually meets a cleaner, asks who they work for, and either receives an answer that matches what the broker said or discovers a misrepresentation that ends the relationship no service recovery can save.

included: restating the service model to every new client-side contact
disclosing crew changes before the client finds out
direct answers about keys, access, badges, certificates and who is on site
keeping complaint-response promises inside what the arrangement actually permits
excluded: the sales-stage disclosure that precedes signature, owned by the acquisition knowledge base
the crew-facing side of the arrangement, owned by the crew sourcing knowledge base
legal opinions about how the arrangement should be characterized

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a client-side contact change, a crew change, or a client question about the service model that the current disclosure record does not already answer

pros.claim: An account built on a model the client actually understands survives the day the client talks to the cleaner directly
pros.example: a facility manager who asks a night cleaner who they work for and hears an answer that matches exactly what the broker described at the last review

cons.claim: Being plain about the model invites the disintermediation question, so the broker must be able to state its own value in a sentence or watch the client try to hire around it
cons.example: an office manager asking why they should not just pay the crew directly, and the broker needing to answer with coverage, supervision, backup and single-invoice accountability rather than with silence

failure_modes: letting shirts, signage or phrasing imply the cleaners are the broker's own staff when the client has not been told the actual arrangement
swapping a crew quietly and letting the client meet strangers in their building
giving vague answers about who holds keys or whose certificate covers the site
acceptance_tests: the account's current day-to-day contact and current signer can each state correctly that contracted crews perform the work and who to call when something is wrong
every crew change at the site has a dated record of when and how the client was told
revisit_triggers: a new client-side contact or signer inherits the account
the crew at the site is replaced or a second crew is added
the client asks to engage the crew directly

nodes.definition: Name, in advance and in writing, the retention moves the broker will not make even when they would work, because they are decided badly under pressure at renewal time. Refused: fear framing that sells cleaning through health scares, invented inspection-failure consequences or manufactured liability threats; relying on a client forgetting their own auto-renew or notice window; burying an escalator so a price change arrives unannounced; timing a price increase to a moment of client distress such as a lost tenant or a leadership change; threatening or allowing service to degrade as negotiating pressure; using keys, access or scheduling as leverage; and pushing an unsophisticated signer - a volunteer treasurer, a church administrator, a sole practitioner - into an extension they have not had the chance to read or ask about. The positive duties that replace them are equally explicit: notice windows and escalator terms are put in front of the client in plain language before the window opens and at a time they can still act; a price change is presented with its mechanism and with options; and a client who wants to test the market is supported with a clean scope document rather than obstructed. The boundary is a first-class control on the repricing and expansion units, not a disclaimer appended to them.

included: the enumerated list of refused retention and repricing levers
the duty to disclose notice windows and escalators before they bite
care proportional to the signer's sophistication
supporting a client's right to rebid
excluded: the mechanics of building the price case, held in the repricing case unit
whether any particular clause is legally enforceable, which is an obligation class for a professional
sales-stage ethics before signature, owned by the acquisition knowledge base

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a client complaint, a lost account post-mortem, or a professional's guidance showing that a practice the broker considered fair was not understood as such by the client

pros.claim: A boundary written before renewal season removes the decision from the moment when losing an account feels unbearable
pros.example: having already decided never to sit on a notice window, so a broker facing a losing month still writes to the client six weeks before their cancellation deadline

cons.claim: Refusing the pressure levers costs accounts that a competitor willing to use them would have held, and the loss is visible while the avoided harm is not
cons.example: a client leaving after being told plainly that their notice window is open, where silence would have locked another year at a workable price

failure_modes: treating the boundary as a values statement that never actually blocks a specific move
letting an urgent cash-flow month justify a one-time exception that becomes the new practice
explaining a renewal term to a sophisticated facilities department the same way as to a volunteer board treasurer and calling both disclosed
acceptance_tests: every price change and renewal in the book can be traced to a dated written notice given to the client before their own notice window opened, in language matched to that signer
no closed or retained account in the last review period was held by a lever on the refused list
revisit_triggers: a competitor's tactic or a cash-flow crisis creates pressure to make an exception
a client turns out not to have understood a renewal or escalator term the broker considered disclosed

nodes.definition: During the life of an account the facts that drive obligation classes keep moving, and the broker's job is to notice and route them rather than to rule on them. The standing watch list: signals that day-to-day dealings with a crew have drifted toward control - setting individual schedules and task order, supplying everything the crew uses, requiring exclusivity, treating a crew member as a de facto employee after a quality problem - which belong to the worker-classification risk class whose tests, thresholds and consequences vary by jurisdiction and change over time and must therefore go to a qualified professional rather than be settled by analogy to another contract; certificates of insurance and any bonding that expire mid-term, or a client's added-insured or endorsement status dropping; site compliance overlays the client introduces after signing, such as a clinic adding a procedure room, a landlord imposing badging and background requirements, or a tenant adding food service; and contract clauses invoked under stress - non-solicitation when a client wants to hire the crew, indemnity after an incident, termination when an exit is contemplated - whose meaning and enforceability are legal questions. The output is a dated register of flags with the account, the trigger, the owner and the referral status, never an in-house opinion recorded as a conclusion.

included: the live-account trigger list for obligation-class review
the dated flag register with owner and referral status
freezing an affected decision until the referral returns
excluded: any determination of how a crew should be classified, which is for a qualified professional in that jurisdiction
the design of the engagement structure itself, owned by the crew sourcing knowledge base
insurance product selection or adequacy opinions

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a change in the working arrangement with a crew, a certificate or endorsement change, a new site compliance requirement, or updated guidance from a qualified professional in the broker's jurisdiction

pros.claim: Catching a control-drift or certificate-lapse signal while it is still a paperwork item keeps it from becoming a dispute discovered after an incident
pros.example: noticing at a routine review that the certificate covering a site expired two months earlier, before an injury or a client audit turns it into a contract breach conversation

cons.claim: Routing every flag to a professional costs time and fees and can stall an operationally obvious fix
cons.example: a quality problem that would be solved by directing the crew's task order sitting unresolved while the control-signal question is checked

failure_modes: assuming a classification or insurance answer carries over from another contract, another site or a prior year
letting an operational remedy quietly increase control signals because it was never routed
recording the broker's own reading of a clause as if it were a resolved legal position
acceptance_tests: every open flag in the register names the account, the triggering fact, the obligation class it touches, the date raised, and whether it has been referred to and answered by a qualified professional
no decision affected by an open flag was executed before the referral returned
revisit_triggers: a client requests exclusive, named or directly-supervised cleaners
a certificate, endorsement or bond approaches expiry or is amended
a client changes the use or compliance regime of the site

nodes.definition: Build the one place where the realized spread actually exists: a per-contract, per-month ledger. On the revenue side it records what was invoiced for the recurring scope plus any periodic or extra work billed, and what was actually collected, along with payment behaviour - late payment, short payment, disputed lines, and any credit or concession issued. On the cost side it records every line the delivery of that site consumed in that month: the crew's payment for the recurring scope, additional or emergency visits, redo and callback labor, consumables and paper the contract makes the broker's responsibility, equipment rental, repair or replacement attributable to the site, subcontracted periodic work, and the broker's own hours spent inspecting, travelling, handling complaints and chasing paperwork for that account. Two capture rules make it usable: cost is booked to the site and the month in which it was incurred rather than the month it was paid, so a callback that ran into a weekend shows against the site that caused it; and every line names its cause, so the read downstream can attribute the variance instead of guessing. The ledger is deliberately modest in ambition - it is not accounting, it is evidence - but nothing else in this knowledge base can be trusted without it.

included: invoiced and collected revenue per contract-month including periodic and extra work
every delivered-cost line attributed to site and month with its cause
payment behaviour, disputes and concessions
the broker's own hours consumed by the account
excluded: statutory bookkeeping, tax treatment and financial statement preparation
crew payment terms and engagement structure, owned by the crew sourcing knowledge base
any benchmark claim about what these lines typically amount to

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a cost line appears that the ledger does not capture, or a monthly variance cannot be attributed from the recorded causes

pros.claim: Attributing costs to the site that caused them makes the expensive accounts visible instead of letting them hide inside a single monthly cost total
pros.example: a site whose repeated Saturday callbacks and drive time appear as its own lines rather than disappearing into an undifferentiated crew payment run

cons.claim: The capture discipline costs administrative time every week and is the first thing abandoned in a busy month, after which the read degrades to memory
cons.example: a broker who stops logging their own complaint-handling hours and then cannot show why an account that looks profitable never leaves them any time

failure_modes: booking costs to the month they were paid rather than the month they were incurred, so a bad month appears one month late
leaving the broker's own hours out entirely so the accounts that consume the most attention appear the cheapest
recording a concession or credit as a revenue reduction with no cause attached, making the variance unattributable
acceptance_tests: for any live contract and any recent month, the ledger returns invoiced revenue, every delivered-cost line with its cause, and the realized spread, without reconstruction from memory
a callback, a special dispatch and a credit issued in the period each appear against the site and month that caused them
revisit_triggers: a new cost line appears that the ledger has no home for, such as equipment brought under the broker or a new consumable responsibility
a month's read cannot be explained from the recorded lines

nodes.definition: Separate the distinct mechanisms by which the cost of delivering the same scope rises after the bid, because each carries a different remedy and treating them as one 'the crew got expensive' problem produces the wrong fix. The mechanisms: a crew renegotiating its rate at its own renewal or under local wage pressure; hours creep, where the building simply takes longer than the bid modeled and the crew has been absorbing the gap until it stops; extra bodies added because the client narrowed the cleaning window and the same work now needs more people in less time; coverage premiums when a regular is absent and a fill-in is slower, unfamiliar or paid more; turnover retraining, where every replacement cleaner runs below the pace of the person they replaced for weeks; consumable consumption drift where the contract puts supplies on the broker and occupancy or traffic grew; travel and fuel on scattered sites; and rework generated by the broker's own inspection findings. The discipline is attribution with evidence - which mechanism, seen how, since when - because a rate renegotiation goes to repricing or re-crewing, an hours miss goes back to the scope model and possibly to a bid-method lesson, coverage churn is a crew-side problem handled under the crew knowledge base, and consumption drift goes to the supplies responsibility term. Remedies that would tighten the broker's direction over a subcontracted crew are routed through the compliance watch before adoption.

included: the named list of post-signature cost-rise mechanisms
attribution of an observed rise to one mechanism with dated evidence
routing each mechanism to its own remedy path
excluded: negotiating with or replacing the crew, which is crew-sourcing work
designing backup coverage, owned by the crew sourcing knowledge base
any claim about what crew rates are or should be

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a crew rate change, a reported hours change, a cleaning-window change, or a consumable consumption shift at a site

pros.claim: Naming the mechanism prevents the default remedy of squeezing the crew, which fixes one month and buys a quality collapse in the next
pros.example: discovering that the rise came from a client narrowing the cleaning window rather than from crew inefficiency, making it a client conversation instead of a crew conversation

cons.claim: Attribution depends on the crew being candid about hours, and a crew afraid of losing the site will under-report the time it actually spends
cons.example: a crew quietly adding an hour a night for months and mentioning it only when asking for more money, leaving the broker with no dated evidence of when the drift began

failure_modes: reading every cost rise as crew opportunism and re-crewing a site whose scope was genuinely under-modeled
accepting a rate increase without asking which mechanism drove it, and so repeating the same miss at the next site
adopting a tighter-supervision remedy without routing the control-signal question to the compliance watch
acceptance_tests: any month where delivered crew cost rose at a site names one dominant mechanism, the evidence that identified it, and the remedy path it was routed to
revisit_triggers: the crew at a site changes, renegotiates, or reports a change in hours
the client changes the cleaning window, occupancy or access arrangements

nodes.definition: Creep is the slow, unbilled expansion of what the crew does, and it is invisible until it is written down in hours. Catalogue the routes it enters by: 'while you're here' requests made directly to the cleaner, which is the most common and least visible route because the cleaner agrees to keep the peace and never tells the broker; areas the client occupied after the walkthrough - a new suite, a converted storage room, an expanded break room, a second-floor tenant fit-out; frequency added informally, such as a Saturday during an audit that never stops; event, move-in and post-construction cleanups treated as included; trash and recycling volume growth as occupancy rises; restrooms or kitchens added to a floor; and periodic work drifting from a billed project into an expectation. Each addition is logged with the date, the requester, what was added, and an estimate of the crew time it consumes, and each is then given one of three explicit dispositions: deliberately absorbed as a recorded goodwill item with an expiry date, traded against an equal task dropped from the scope, or converted into a change order and billed. The fourth disposition - silent absorption that nobody recorded - is the one this unit exists to eliminate, because it is the mechanism by which a contract that was priced correctly at the walkthrough becomes unprofitable without a single visible decision.

included: the entry routes creep uses, including requests made directly to the cleaner
dated logging with requester and estimated added crew time
the three permitted dispositions and the ban on silent absorption
excluded: writing the change order itself, held in the change-order unit
the original scope document and its task and frequency matrix, owned by the acquisition knowledge base
instructing the crew on how to perform the added task, which is crew-side work

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a reported out-of-scope request, an occupancy or floor-area change at the site, or a goodwill item reaching its expiry date

pros.claim: A dated log turns a vague feeling that the account got heavier into a provable list that a client will recognize and accept at a repricing conversation
pros.example: presenting six logged additions with dates and requesters at a renewal review rather than asserting that 'the building has grown' and being contradicted

cons.claim: Logging depends on the cleaner reporting requests they were asked to keep quiet, and building that reporting habit takes patience and costs goodwill with the client-side asker
cons.example: a receptionist who has been asking the cleaner for extra kitchen duty being told politely that the request now goes through the broker

failure_modes: logging additions only at renewal, when memory has lost the dates and the client can reasonably deny them
granting goodwill items with no expiry so a favour becomes an obligation nobody can withdraw
counting a one-off event cleanup as permanent creep and overstating the case for a price change
acceptance_tests: every addition in the log carries a date, a requester, an estimate of added crew time, and one of the three permitted dispositions with no entry left undisposed
goodwill items carry an expiry date and are re-decided rather than rolling forward silently
revisit_triggers: a cleaner or supervisor reports being asked for work outside the scope document
the client occupies new space, adds an event, or changes occupancy at the site

nodes.definition: Read each contract's month by comparing the realized spread in the ledger against what the bid model expected, then decompose the gap rather than reporting a single direction. The decomposition uses the named mechanisms so the answer is actionable: crew cost drift, scope creep, complaint-driven rework and dispatches, periodic work timing, billing errors and unbilled extras, and concessions issued. Periodic timing deserves its own discipline because it is the most common false alarm in this business - a quarterly floor refinish or an annual carpet extraction lands in one month and makes a healthy account look collapsed, so project work is smoothed across the term before a band is assigned and single-month reads taken during a project month are marked unreliable. The output per contract is a band - healthy, thin, eroding, under water - with the dominant mechanism named and a corrective owner assigned, plus a note of how many consecutive reads the band has held, because a single bad month is noise and a trend is a decision. The band, not the raw number, is what the rest of the system consumes: one identified cause on an eroding account routes to a change order or a crew conversation, while several causes on an under-water account route to the repricing case or the exit ladder.

included: comparison of realized spread against the bid model per contract-month
decomposition into named mechanisms with a dominant one identified
smoothing periodic work across the term before banding
band assignment with consecutive-read count and corrective owner
excluded: capturing the underlying cost lines, held in the ledger unit
deciding the commercial response, held in the scorecard, repricing and exit units
any statement of what band a contract type should sit in

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: two consecutive reads in a new band, a change order taking effect, or a rescope that replaces the bid model the read compares against

pros.claim: Decomposing the variance means the remedy addresses the actual mechanism rather than the most emotionally available one
pros.example: an account that looked like a crew problem resolving into three logged scope additions and one billing error, changing the response from re-crewing to a change order

cons.claim: A monthly cadence can act too slowly on a fast collapse and too quickly on lumpy accounts, so band changes need a consecutive-read rule that inevitably lags
cons.example: a site whose crew quit mid-month showing a normal band until the following read, by which time the client has already escalated

failure_modes: reading a project month as a collapse and re-crewing or repricing an account that was never unhealthy
reporting a single 'margin down' number with no mechanism, which produces action aimed at whoever is easiest to blame
letting an eroding band sit with no assigned corrective owner until it becomes an under-water band
acceptance_tests: every live contract has a current band, a named dominant mechanism, a corrective owner, and a count of consecutive reads at that band
months containing periodic project work are smoothed or explicitly marked unreliable before a band change is made
revisit_triggers: a band moves in either direction for two consecutive reads
a change order, crew change or client-side building change lands at the site
the bid model for the site is superseded by a rescope

nodes.definition: The retention engine starts with capture, and capture fails when complaints live in five places. Every route a complaint can arrive by is funneled into one dated record: a text to the broker's mobile at eleven at night, an email to a shared inbox, a note in a logbook left at the site, a remark made to the cleaner in the corridor, a comment dropped at a review meeting, and a ticket raised in the client's own facilities system. Each record carries site, area, task, reporter, reporter's role, what was actually observed rather than the adjective used, and the service date it refers to. Triage then assigns severity with rules written in advance: a safety, biohazard, or lock-up and security failure jumps the queue and is handled the same day regardless of cost; a visible miss in a client-facing area such as lobby glass, entry mats or a restroom is a next-service item; and a low-grade recurring gripe such as dusting detail is a pattern item that goes to the trend rather than to an emergency dispatch. Triage also starts the acknowledgement clock, which is the single most visible retention behaviour the broker controls and is a promise about how fast a human replies, never a promise about how fast the building changes. Complaints raised by the crew itself - a room locked all week, a blocked area, an unsafe condition, a missing key - enter the same log, because they are the early warning that a client complaint is coming.

included: funnelling every arrival channel into one dated log
the observed-fact record with site, area, task and reporter role
written severity rules and the acknowledgement clock
crew-raised issues logged as leading indicators
excluded: diagnosing the cause, held in the root-cause unit
correcting the work, which is crew execution under the crew knowledge base
quality inspection scoring, designed in the crew knowledge base and consumed here

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a complaint surfaces that never entered the log, or a new arrival channel appears at a client site

pros.claim: One log with one clock converts scattered irritation into a queue that can be worked, and makes the account's real complaint history visible at renewal
pros.example: producing at a review the full dated list of the year's complaints and their closure times instead of the client's recollection of 'constant problems'

cons.claim: Formal intake can make a previously casual client feel bureaucratic, and some contacts will keep using the channel they like regardless
cons.example: a facility manager who prefers texting the cleaner directly and resents being asked to email the broker, requiring the broker to log the text on their behalf rather than insist

failure_modes: complaints living in a phone's message history where they cannot be counted or trended
recording the client's adjective rather than the observed fact, so the record cannot be verified later
starting the clock at the moment the broker noticed rather than the moment the client reported
acceptance_tests: every complaint from any channel in the period exists as one dated record with site, area, task, reporter role and observed fact, and carries a severity class from the written rules
crew-raised site issues appear in the same log with the same clock
revisit_triggers: complaints are found that never entered the log
a new client-side reporting channel appears, such as the client's own facilities ticketing system

nodes.definition: Before any correction is dispatched, assign the complaint to exactly one cause class, because the class decides both the remedy and who bears the cost. The classes: scope gap, where the task was never in the contract at all and the client has been assuming it - interior windows, blind cleaning, inside the refrigerator, the loading dock; spec ambiguity, where the task exists but the standard was never defined, so 'clean restrooms' means detail-level to the client and a wipe-down to the crew; execution failure, where the task is in scope, defined, and the crew simply missed it; coverage failure, where the crew was absent, short-handed or rushed by a shortened window; supplies or equipment failure, such as no liner stock, an exhausted dispenser or a dead vacuum; expectation drift, where the building's use changed - occupancy doubled, a tenant added a gym or food service, a hybrid schedule moved the soil pattern - so identical work now reads as insufficient; and client-side cause, such as a spill after service, a contractor's dust, or an event nobody told the crew about. Routing follows the class: execution and coverage failures are corrected free and fast and go to the crew accountability process owned by the crew knowledge base; spec ambiguity goes back to the scope document as a definition fix; supplies failure goes to the responsibility model; and scope gap and expectation drift become commercial conversations that may end in a change order or a repricing case. The expensive error is misclassification in either direction: billing a client for the broker's own execution failure, or re-cleaning free forever what was never sold.

included: the seven cause classes and their distinguishing evidence
single-class assignment before dispatch
the routing rule from class to remedy and to who bears the cost
excluded: disciplining or replacing the crew, owned by the crew sourcing knowledge base
writing the resulting change order, held in the change-order unit
the original scope document's construction, owned by the acquisition knowledge base

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a disputed classification, or a repeating complaint whose assigned class keeps changing across months

pros.claim: Classifying before dispatching stops the broker from converting an out-of-scope task into a permanent free obligation through repeated goodwill re-cleans
pros.example: recognizing that the interior windows being complained about were never in the task matrix, so the response is a priced add-on offer rather than a third free clean

cons.claim: Classification takes a beat, and a client in a bad mood experiences any diagnosis before action as an argument about blame
cons.example: a client hearing 'that was never in the scope' at the moment of complaint and reading it as a refusal, when the same fact delivered after an immediate correction would have been accepted

failure_modes: defaulting every complaint to execution failure because it is the fastest thing to say to an angry client
using scope gap as a shield for genuine quality problems, which accelerates cancellation
assigning two classes and therefore no clear remedy owner
acceptance_tests: each closed complaint in the period carries exactly one cause class and the evidence that supported it, and the remedy taken matches the routing rule for that class
no complaint classed as scope gap or expectation drift was corrected free more than the recorded goodwill allowance without a change order or a documented decision
revisit_triggers: the same area or task generates complaints under different classes across months
a client disputes a classification or a charge that followed from one

nodes.definition: The loop that retains clients has four stages and fails if any one is skipped. Acknowledge: a human reply inside the promised window that names who is handling it and what will happen next, sent even when the answer is not yet known - silence in the first hours does more damage than the original miss. Correct: a specific instruction to the crew naming the area, the task and the deadline, with the vehicle chosen by severity - the next scheduled service for routine misses, a special dispatch for safety, security or client-facing failures - and with the instruction routed through whatever channel the engagement structure supports rather than by direct supervision that would raise a control-signal flag. Verify: the broker or its inspector confirms the correction physically or by dated photographic evidence rather than accepting a 'done', because an unverified closure that the client discovers is worse than no closure at all. Close: tell the complainant what was found, what was corrected, and what changed so it does not recur, in writing, even when the finding is unflattering to the broker. Every loop also records what the correction consumed - a special dispatch, an unpaid re-clean, the broker's drive time, a credit issued - and posts it to the ledger, because in volume those corrections are themselves a reason a contract is under water, and a retention engine nobody costs will quietly eat the spread it was meant to protect.

included: the four mandatory stages and their evidence
severity-driven choice of correction vehicle
verification before closure and written closure to the complainant
posting the correction's cost to the ledger
excluded: how the crew performs the corrective cleaning
crew accountability and replacement decisions, owned by the crew sourcing knowledge base
any promise of a response time stated as an industry standard

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a re-opened complaint, a slipped acknowledgement window, or correction costs at a site rising far enough to change its margin band

pros.claim: Written closure converts a bad night into evidence of reliability, which is the single most durable retention asset the broker owns
pros.example: a client who was ready to rebid producing, months later, the broker's closure notes as the reason they stayed through a leadership change

cons.claim: Fast, generous correction is expensive and, applied to every class of complaint, subsidizes work that was never sold
cons.example: repeated special dispatches to re-clean an area that a change order should have covered, each one recorded as a cost against an account that then reads as unprofitable

failure_modes: correcting the work but never telling the complainant, so the client's memory records only the problem
trusting a verbal 'it's done' and being contradicted by the client the next morning
letting correction costs go unrecorded so the retention engine's true cost never appears in the margin read
acceptance_tests: every complaint closed in the period shows an acknowledgement inside the promised window, a dated correction instruction, verification evidence, and a written closure message to the complainant
the cost of each correction appears against the site and month in the ledger
revisit_triggers: a closed complaint re-opens or the same area fails again within the same period
acknowledgement times slip at any site
correction costs at a site become a visible line in its margin read

nodes.definition: A single complaint is an event; the load is the signal. Normalize each site's complaints against its size, service frequency and fixture density so a seven-night medical building is not judged by the same raw count as a small twice-weekly office, then read four things: direction across months, concentration by area or task (a restroom that generates a third of a site's complaints is a crew instruction problem, not a client problem), the share of complaints that re-open after closure - a re-open being worth several fresh complaints as a warning - and the reporting altitude, meaning whether complaints now arrive from the property manager or the client's executive rather than from the day-to-day contact, which shows the issue has already escalated past the person who used to absorb it. Rising load predicts two costs at once, and that is why it belongs in this knowledge base rather than only in a quality system: it forecasts cancellation, and it forecasts margin erosion that is already visible in the ledger as dispatches, re-cleans and broker hours. Read early, it buys the months needed to re-crew, rescope or reprice before a cancellation notice arrives; read late, it explains a loss the broker could no longer prevent.

included: normalization for site size, frequency and fixture density
trend direction, area concentration, re-open share and reporting altitude
linking complaint load to correction cost already in the ledger
excluded: inspection and quality scoring methodology, designed in the crew knowledge base
the individual complaint's remedy, held in the response loop
predicting churn for any account outside the broker's own logged history

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a re-opened complaint, two consecutive rises in normalized load, a change in reporting altitude, or a previously vocal site falling silent

pros.claim: Normalized load makes accounts comparable, so attention goes to the site that is actually deteriorating rather than the one that is simply large
pros.example: a big multi-floor account with many small logged items reading healthier than a small clinic whose three complaints all re-opened in one month

cons.claim: Complaint counts measure reporting behaviour as much as cleaning quality, so a silent client can look healthy right up to the cancellation letter
cons.example: an account with no complaints for months whose contact had simply stopped bothering to report and had already begun collecting competing bids

failure_modes: comparing raw counts across sites of different size and frequency and mis-ranking the book
treating a re-opened complaint as just another entry rather than as the strongest warning in the log
ignoring the shift in reporting altitude until the escalation is already at the signer
acceptance_tests: each site has a normalized load trend covering at least three reads, with its area concentration, re-open share and reporting altitude recorded
a site whose load is rising has a named next action and owner before the next read
revisit_triggers: a site's normalized load rises for two consecutive reads or any complaint re-opens
a site goes unusually silent after a period of regular reporting
complaints begin arriving from above the day-to-day contact

nodes.definition: An account is held by people, and the people change more often than the building does. Map three roles per account and keep them current: who signs and can cancel (an owner, an office manager, a property manager, a board or a regional facilities buyer), who the crew and broker deal with day to day (a receptionist, a site supervisor, a tenant representative, a night security lead), and who sponsors the relationship - the person who chose the broker and whose own credibility is attached to that choice. Record the state of each as reachable, responsive, satisfied, or gone. The dangerous transitions are specific and recognisable in advance: the sponsor leaves and a successor arrives with a preferred vendor or a mandate to cut costs; a property-management company takes over the building and re-bids every service contract as a matter of routine; the client is acquired, consolidates sites, or moves purchasing to a regional office that has never met the broker; a new day-to-day contact begins formally logging issues the previous one handled with a phone call; or the sponsor is promoted and stops paying attention. Each transition triggers the same first move - re-introduce the service model, re-walk the scope with the new person, agree in writing what 'good' looks like at this site, and bring the next service review forward - because an inherited contact judges the account by what they see this month and has heard none of the history that earned the last three years.

included: the three roles, their current state, and how they are kept current
the named dangerous transitions and their early signals
the re-onboarding first move for a new contact
excluded: the sales-stage buying-process map used to win the contract, owned by the acquisition knowledge base
the meeting mechanics of the service review, held in the review unit
storing personal information about contacts beyond what running the account requires

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a change in any mapped role, a building ownership or management change, or a client reorganization that moves purchasing

pros.claim: Knowing who sponsors the account tells the broker whose departure is a genuine emergency and whose is routine
pros.example: the office manager who selected the broker leaving being treated as a same-week priority, while a receptionist change is handled at the next scheduled visit

cons.claim: Relationship state is judged subjectively and can flatter the broker, especially with a polite contact who is already shopping
cons.example: recording a contact as satisfied because calls are pleasant, while procurement has already issued a request for proposals the broker never sees

failure_modes: knowing only the day-to-day contact and never meeting the person who can actually cancel
discovering a management-company takeover from the crew rather than from the client
treating a new contact as a continuation of the old relationship instead of re-onboarding them
acceptance_tests: every live account names its signer, day-to-day contact and sponsor with a current state and the date last verified
every contact change in the period has a dated re-onboarding record covering the service model, a scope re-walk and an agreed definition of good
revisit_triggers: any of the three roles changes, becomes unreachable, or stops responding
the building changes ownership or management company
the client is acquired, merges sites or centralizes purchasing

nodes.definition: Hold a recurring client review that presents evidence instead of asking 'how are we doing?', a question that invites either polite silence or an ambush. The pack is assembled from records that already exist: inspection scores produced by the quality process designed in the crew knowledge base and consumed here, the complaint log with response and closure times, periodic and project work completed and scheduled ahead, scope changes agreed since the last review, crew changes and how they were communicated, and anything about the building that changed - occupancy, tenants, hours, construction. Cadence is proportional to value and fragility: a multi-site portfolio, a new account in its first months, or a site with a rising complaint load earns frequent reviews, while a stable small office may need only an annual one, and the broker's own supervisory capacity caps how many any book can support. Placement matters as much as frequency: reviews are scheduled deliberately ahead of the renewal and notice windows so goodwill and evidence exist before any price conversation rather than being manufactured during it. The review is also the honest venue for early warning - telling a client months ahead that cost pressure is building, and what the broker is doing about it, is the difference between a negotiated repricing and an ambush that triggers a rebid.

included: the evidence pack and where each item comes from
cadence proportional to account value, fragility and broker capacity
placement relative to renewal and notice windows
early warning of cost pressure
excluded: designing inspections and quality scores, owned by the crew sourcing knowledge base
the price case itself, held in the repricing case unit
the expansion offer, held in the expansion unit and merely occasioned here

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a contact change, a band or complaint-load change at the account, or a change in the broker's supervisory capacity

pros.claim: A review that arrives with the year's complaint closures and inspection record makes the broker's reliability a documented fact rather than a claim
pros.example: a new facility manager reading the closure log from before their arrival and concluding that the misses they inherited were already handled

cons.claim: Reviews consume the broker's scarcest resource and can surface dormant dissatisfaction that would otherwise never have been raised
cons.example: a quarterly meeting where a client, prompted to think about the service, produces a list of small irritations that then requires real corrective work

failure_modes: holding reviews only when something is wrong, which trains the client to expect bad news
scheduling the first review after the notice window has already opened
presenting opinions and reassurance instead of the inspection, complaint and periodic-work record
acceptance_tests: every account has a next review date set relative to its renewal and notice window, and a cadence justified by its value and fragility
each held review produced a dated pack containing inspection scores, complaint closures, periodic work status and scope changes since the last one
revisit_triggers: a contact change, a rising complaint load, or a band change at the account
the broker's supervisory capacity changes so the promised cadence is no longer deliverable

nodes.definition: Combine four independent readings into one per-account state, because each alone misleads: the margin band from the health read, the complaint trend from the load signal, the relationship state from the map, and the contract runway - months to term end or notice window - together with payment behaviour. What makes this unit useful is that the pairs matter more than the parts, and the pairs prescribe different actions. Profitable with a deteriorating relationship is the account to visit this week, because the money is real and the risk is the person. Unprofitable with a delighted client is the best repricing case in the book and should be scheduled before its window opens. Unprofitable with an already-unhappy client is an exit candidate rather than a rescue project, because the broker would have to spend to fix quality and then ask for more money from someone with no goodwill left. Profitable, healthy and expiring soon is the expansion and early-renewal target. Thin margin with a rising complaint load is a crew decision before it is a price decision. The output is a ranked queue with exactly one owner and one next step per account, refreshed on the same cadence as the margin read, so the book is managed by state rather than by whoever complained most recently or shouted loudest.

included: the four input readings and how they combine
the named pair states and the action each prescribes
a ranked queue with one owner and one next step per account
excluded: the underlying measurement of each input, held in their own units
executing the prescribed action, held in the repricing, expansion and exit units
any claim about what share of a book should sit in a given state

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a change in any input reading, a calendar alarm, or an obligation-class flag opened against an account

pros.claim: Pairing money with relationship stops two symmetrical mistakes: rescuing accounts that should be exited and neglecting profitable accounts that are quietly slipping away
pros.example: a well-paying account with a departed sponsor rising above a noisy but stable low-margin site in the same week's queue

cons.claim: A composite state can hide a single severe reading, and a queue creates the illusion that the lower half is safe
cons.example: an account whose margin and relationship look adequate while an unresolved obligation-class flag sits underneath, ranked too low to be looked at

failure_modes: collapsing the four readings into one number and losing the pair logic that drives the action
refreshing the queue too rarely to be actionable, so it becomes a report rather than a work list
leaving accounts with no owner, which means the queue is read and nothing happens
acceptance_tests: every live account carries a current margin band, complaint trend, relationship state and runway, plus one named owner and one next step
the queue is refreshed on the same cadence as the margin read and its top items show dated action since the previous refresh
revisit_triggers: any input reading changes band or state at any account
a renewal, notice or certificate alarm fires
an obligation-class flag is opened against an account

nodes.definition: Every agreed change - an added area, an added service night, a new task, a task removed, a periodic service moving into the recurring scope, a frequency reduction the client asks for to save money - becomes one written change order that updates three things at the same moment: the client's price and the invoice that follows it, the crew's scope document and what the crew is paid for the new work, and the site's cost model in the ledger so the next margin read compares against reality. Updating one without the others produces the two most common self-inflicted losses in this business: the crew is asked to do more while the invoice stays where it was, which turns a good crew into a resentful one and then into a quality problem; or the price rises while the crew's instructions never change, which the client notices immediately and reasonably calls dishonest. The change order states what changes, from what date, what it costs, what it replaces if anything, and who approved it on the client side - a person with authority to bind the account, not the receptionist who made the request. Small goodwill items may still be granted without one, but only with a recorded expiry date, so that a favour cannot silently mature into a permanent obligation the next renewal has to price around.

included: the three simultaneous updates and their effective date
the authority requirement for client-side approval
goodwill items granted with a recorded expiry
scope reductions handled by the same instrument
excluded: drafting the underlying contract terms, owned by the acquisition knowledge base
how the crew performs the added work
the price case for a general increase, held in the repricing case unit

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an undisposed scope addition at the next read, a disputed charge, or a goodwill item reaching its expiry date

pros.claim: Simultaneous updates keep the crew's instructions, the client's invoice and the margin model describing the same building
pros.example: an added second-floor suite appearing in the crew's task list, on the invoice and in the site's cost model from the same effective date, so the next read is not polluted by an unexplained cost rise

cons.claim: Insisting on paperwork for small changes slows the responsiveness clients value and can make an easy yes feel like a negotiation
cons.example: a client asking for one extra bin pickup and receiving a change order for signature, where a recorded goodwill item with an expiry would have preserved both the relationship and the record

failure_modes: changing the client's price without changing the crew's scope, which the client detects and never forgets
adding to the crew's scope without adding to the price, the most common route from a profitable contract to a losing one
accepting approval from someone without authority and then being unable to collect
acceptance_tests: every change order in the period shows a matching price update, crew scope update and ledger cost-model update with the same effective date, plus a named approver with authority
every goodwill item granted without a change order carries an expiry date and a decision at that date
revisit_triggers: a logged scope addition remains undisposed at the next margin read
a client disputes a charge that followed a change order
a goodwill item reaches its expiry

nodes.definition: Every live contract carries dates that silently decide the broker's options, and a broker who learns them from the client is already too late. The calendar holds, per account: the term end, any auto-renew trigger and the date it fires, the notice period each side must give and therefore the last day action is possible, any anniversary or index date that opens an escalator or adjustment, insurance certificate and bond expiries, and the client's own budget cycle, which often constrains when a price change can even be discussed regardless of what the contract permits. Each date carries a lead-time alarm set far enough ahead to actually do something - hold a service review, fix a quality problem, assemble a repricing case, re-crew a site, or prepare a transition - rather than an alarm that merely announces the deadline. Two boundaries define this unit. First, interpretation is not its business: what a clause requires, whether an auto-renew is enforceable, and what a notice must contain are obligation-class questions for a qualified professional in that jurisdiction, and the calendar records the referral rather than a ruling. Second, the calendar is never used as a weapon - the client is told about their own notice window plainly and in time, because a renewal obtained through the client's forgetfulness is exactly the lever this knowledge base refuses.

included: term, auto-renew, notice, escalator, certificate and budget-cycle dates per account
lead-time alarms sized to the work they must trigger
recording clause questions as referrals rather than rulings
proactive disclosure of the client's own notice window
excluded: drafting or negotiating the clauses themselves, owned by the acquisition knowledge base
any opinion on enforceability, which is an obligation class for a professional
the content of the price case, held in the repricing case unit

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a contract amendment or replacement, a certificate renewal or lapse, or a change in the client's budget cycle

pros.claim: Lead-time alarms convert renewals from events that happen to the broker into work the broker schedules months ahead
pros.example: an alarm months before a notice window opening the sequence of a service review, a margin read and a decision, so the renewal conversation happens on the broker's timetable

cons.claim: A calendar is only as true as the contract files behind it, and books assembled over years contain accounts whose signed terms are missing, amended by email, or never countersigned
cons.example: discovering at an alarm that the only surviving document for a site is a proposal the client accepted by reply, with no term or notice provision at all

failure_modes: letting an auto-renew fire unexamined and locking a term at a price the ledger already shows as losing
setting alarms at the deadline rather than at the point where action is still possible
recording the broker's own reading of a notice clause as if it were settled
acceptance_tests: every live account has its term end, renewal trigger, notice period, any escalator date and its certificate expiries entered, each with a lead-time alarm long enough for the work it must trigger
each alarm that fired in the period shows the decision it produced and the date the client was informed of any window affecting them
revisit_triggers: a contract is amended, extended, or replaced by a new document
a certificate, endorsement or bond is renewed or lapses
a client's budget cycle or fiscal year changes

nodes.definition: A price increase that survives contact with a facility manager is an evidence package, not a percentage. Assemble four strands: the documented cost drivers with dates, drawn from the drift diagnosis and the ledger - a crew rate change, hours the ledger shows the site actually consumes, consumable consumption as occupancy grew, added travel; the scope additions logged since signing with their requesters and estimated hours, which are usually the most persuasive strand because the client recognizes their own requests; the service record that earns the right to ask, meaning inspection scores, complaint closures and periodic work delivered on schedule; and the building changes that moved the work, such as new tenants, extended hours, or a fit-out. Then construct options rather than a single demand, because a client with choices negotiates while a client with an ultimatum rebids: hold the price and reduce frequency or scope; hold the scope and adjust the price; restructure - move a periodic service to as-needed, shift supplies responsibility, change service days or the cleaning window to a cheaper delivery pattern; or phase a change across the term. Every option is costed with its own delivered-cost model so the broker knows which ones it can actually staff and at what spread, because an option offered and then withdrawn as unaffordable does more damage than never offering it. Price reductions belong here too: when a building genuinely got lighter, the honest case runs in the same format in the client's favour.

included: the four evidence strands with dates and sources
option construction including scope reduction, restructuring and phasing
a delivered-cost model per option
the symmetrical case for a price reduction when work genuinely fell
excluded: the conversation itself, held in the repricing conversation unit
the original bid math, owned by the acquisition knowledge base
any assertion of a standard or typical increase

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a change in a documented cost driver, a disputed scope addition, or a client budget or building change that alters which options are viable

pros.claim: Options convert a confrontation into a purchasing decision the client can win something in, which is what keeps the contract from going out to bid
pros.example: a client who cannot fund an increase choosing a reduced Friday-only frequency and staying, instead of tendering the whole contract to test the market

cons.claim: Building a full evidence pack takes hours the broker does not have for every account, and a thin pack is worse than none because it invites the client to dispute the strongest claim
cons.example: presenting three undated scope additions the client's own contact does not remember requesting and losing credibility for the whole case

failure_modes: leading with a percentage and assembling the justification afterwards
offering an option the crew cannot actually staff at the quoted delivery pattern
omitting the service record, so the case reads as a demand from a vendor with nothing to show
acceptance_tests: each case names its cost drivers with dates and sources, its logged scope additions, the service record it rests on, and at least two options each carrying its own delivered-cost model
no option in the pack lacks a staffing check confirming it can be delivered as described
revisit_triggers: a cost driver changes between building the case and the meeting
the client's budget cycle or a building change alters which options are viable
a logged scope addition in the pack is disputed

nodes.definition: Run the conversation with the person who can decide, early in their budget cycle and well before the notice window, in person where the account justifies it. Open with the service record and the mechanism - what changed in the building and in delivered cost, with dates - rather than with the number, then present the options and their trade-offs plainly, including which of them the broker prefers and why. The refused levers are the ones from the ethical boundary and they matter most here, where the temptation is highest: no health or inspection-failure framing, no urgency manufactured by having sat on the notice window, no hint that the standard will slip if the increase is refused, no approach to a signer who lacks authority in the hope of an easier yes, and no exploitation of a client in visible distress. Expect the standard responses and prepare honest answers: 'we'll get other bids' is legitimate and is met by supplying a clean scope document so competitors quote the same work rather than a cheaper one; 'we can't afford it this year' is the scope-reduction option, priced honestly and with the consequences stated; and silence is met with one scheduled written follow-up ahead of the notice window, not with repeated pressure. Set the walk-away before the meeting - the spread below which the broker will let the contract go, decided from the ledger while calm - so the concession ladder has a floor that the fear of losing an account in the room cannot move.

included: timing, venue and audience selection
opening with record and mechanism rather than a number
prepared honest answers to rebid, affordability and silence
the pre-set walk-away spread and concession floor
excluded: assembling the evidence, held in the case construction unit
new-business negotiation with prospects, owned by the acquisition knowledge base
any claim about how much of an increase a client will accept

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a rebid request, a change of decision-maker, or an outcome where the client's response did not match any prepared answer

pros.claim: A walk-away decided in advance keeps a bad concession from being made in the room, where losing the account feels worse than losing money
pros.example: a broker holding at the recorded floor and offering a frequency reduction instead of accepting a price that the ledger already showed would deliver nothing

cons.claim: Honest, early conversations sometimes hand the client the idea of testing the market before they had thought of it
cons.example: a client responding to a well-argued increase by tendering the contract, and a competitor buying it at a price the broker would not match

failure_modes: opening with the number, which turns the meeting into a negotiation about a figure with no context
conceding below the recorded floor because the meeting is going badly
delivering the case to a contact with no authority and calling the account handled
acceptance_tests: each repricing conversation record shows the date relative to the notice window, who attended and their authority, the options presented, the walk-away recorded before the meeting, and the outcome
