no outcome in the period shows a concession below the pre-set floor without a written re-decision made outside the meeting
revisit_triggers: a client requests a rebid or invites competitors
the decision-maker changes between the case being built and the meeting
a concession below the floor is contemplated

nodes.definition: Existing accounts are the cheapest place to add recurring revenue - the building is known, access is solved, the crew is already on site, and the trust exists - provided the expansion is earned rather than pushed. Map the ladder per account: added frequency, such as a fourth or fifth night, weekend coverage, or a second daily restroom check in a high-traffic building; periodic and project services the client is currently buying elsewhere or not at all, including floor stripping and refinishing, burnishing, carpet extraction, interior window cleaning, high dusting, pressure washing and post-construction cleanups; daytime presence such as a day porter for lobbies, restrooms and events in a busy building; consumable supply programmes where the contract structure allows it; adjacent areas the client occupies but never added; and sister sites inside the same client - other branches, other buildings in the same portfolio, or the property manager's other properties. Sequencing is the discipline: expansion is offered from demonstrated performance rather than from need, which usually means after a clean service review and never during an open complaint; it is priced with the same delivered-cost mechanism as any new work rather than discounted to buy goodwill, because a discounted add-on drags the whole account's spread down permanently; it is checked against crew capacity and capability before it is offered, since an expansion the crew cannot absorb converts a healthy account into a complaint generator; and it is never bundled with a price increase, which would turn an offer into a lever.

included: the expansion ladder from frequency through periodic services, day porter, supplies, adjacent areas and sister sites
sequencing by demonstrated performance and crew capacity
pricing add-ons by the same delivered-cost mechanism
the rule against bundling expansion with a price increase
excluded: winning a brand-new client, owned by the acquisition knowledge base
recruiting crews or capability for a service the broker cannot yet deliver, owned by the crew sourcing knowledge base
any figure describing what expansion is worth

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a change in the account's health state, a change in crew capacity or capability, or the client acquiring space or sites

pros.claim: Expansion inside a healthy account adds recurring revenue without the acquisition cost, the walkthrough cycle or the access setup a new site demands
pros.example: adding quarterly carpet extraction and a day porter to a building the crew already services nightly, using the same keys, the same supervisor and the same invoice

cons.claim: Expansion increases concentration in one client, so a single relationship failure now removes several revenue lines at once
cons.example: a portfolio where added periodic work and two sister sites all sit under one property manager whose departure puts the whole cluster into a rebid

failure_modes: offering an add-on during an open complaint, which reads as tone-deaf and damages the recovery
discounting the add-on to win it and permanently diluting the account's spread
selling a periodic service the crew cannot perform to standard and generating a complaint at a previously clean site
acceptance_tests: each expansion offered in the period was made from a documented clean service record with no open complaint, was priced by the same delivered-cost mechanism as new work, and passed a crew capacity and capability check before it was offered
no expansion offer in the period was presented in the same conversation as a price increase
revisit_triggers: an account's health state changes after an expansion is offered but before it is delivered
crew capacity or capability changes in the territory
the client acquires new space or new sites

nodes.definition: Exit is the last rung of a ladder that must be climbed in order, and skipping rungs is how brokers lose contracts they could have kept and keep contracts they should have released. Rung one: verify the loss is real in the ledger rather than an artifact of periodic-work timing, a billing error, or an unbilled change order. Rung two: bill the creep - convert the logged additions into change orders and see what the account looks like priced for the work actually being done. Rung three: address delivered cost - re-crew the site, restructure the delivery pattern, or move supplies responsibility, each with a deadline and an owner. Rung four: reprice or rescope at the earliest legitimate window with the case and the options. Exit is chosen when those are exhausted or refused, when delivered cost cannot be brought below any price the client will pay, when complaint load makes the site unservable at a price any crew will accept, or when an obligation-class flag cannot be satisfied. The exit itself is an operational act with duties: honor the contract's notice terms with the wording checked by a qualified professional where anything is unclear, tell the client before telling anyone else and give a professional reason without disparaging them or the crew, offer a transition window and - if asked - a clean scope document so their next vendor can quote the real work, tell the crew early enough that they can replace the income, and return keys, badges, alarm codes and access cards against a signed receipt. Abandonment, and its quieter cousin of letting service decay until the client cancels, are refused outright: they harm the client, the crew and the referral base that produces the next contract.

included: the ordered remedy ladder and its verification rung
the named exit triggers
exit duties covering notice, client-first communication, transition, crew notice and access return
the explicit refusal of abandonment and service decay
excluded: interpreting the termination clause, which is an obligation class for a qualified professional
replacing the lost revenue, which is acquisition work
the crew's own transition arrangements, owned by the crew sourcing knowledge base

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a remedy deadline passing without result, an unresolvable obligation-class flag, or a crew withdrawal that leaves the site unservable at any workable price

pros.claim: An ordered ladder means most under-water accounts are fixed rather than lost, and the ones that do end are ended on terms that protect the broker's reputation
pros.example: an account that looked terminal being restored by billing eight logged additions and moving one periodic service to as-needed, with no price conversation needed at all

cons.claim: Climbing every rung costs months of management attention, and a broker with limited capacity can spend a quarter rescuing one site while three healthy accounts go unreviewed
cons.example: a remedy programme at one losing building consuming the review cycle in which a profitable account's sponsor quietly left

failure_modes: exiting on one bad read that a change order or a project-month correction would have explained
holding a losing contract indefinitely because cancelling feels like failure, while it starves the accounts that pay
degrading service or going silent to force the client to cancel, which converts a clean exit into a reputational loss
acceptance_tests: every exit in the period shows the ladder rungs attempted with dates and owners before the exit decision, and the trigger that fired
every exit shows notice given per the contract, the client informed first, a transition offer, dated crew notice, and a signed record of returned keys, badges and access credentials
revisit_triggers: an account sits under water for consecutive reads with no remedy owner
a remedy deadline passes without result
an obligation-class flag on the account cannot be resolved

nodes.definition: Every account that cancels, nearly cancels and is saved, or is exited by the broker gets the same short structured review, held while the people involved still remember the detail. The questions are fixed so the answers are comparable across the book: what was the first true warning signal, and how many months before the end did it appear; which unit should have caught it - the ledger, the margin read, the complaint loop, the relationship map, or the renewal calendar - and why did it not; was the root cause priced in at bid time (a scope or production assumption wrong from the first month), delivered (a crew that could not hold the standard, or a coverage model that failed), relational (a sponsor left, a management company took over), or commercial (a competitor bought the work at a price the broker declined to match); what did the save attempt cost in dispatches, credits and broker hours; and what would be done differently. Findings are then routed deliberately out of this knowledge base rather than filed: pricing, scoping and production assumptions go back to the bid method; crew selection, quality and coverage failures go to the crew sourcing and quality method; and retention-process failures stay here as concrete changes to the response loop, the review cadence or the scorecard's thresholds. Without this loop a broker re-sells the same building class at the same wrong price to the same kind of buyer and calls the recurring outcome bad luck.

included: the fixed question set applied to losses, saves and exits alike
attribution to priced-in, delivered, relational or commercial root causes
the cost of the save attempt
routing findings to the bid method, the crew method, or back into this one
excluded: implementing the bid-method or crew-method changes themselves, which belong to those knowledge bases
attributing blame to an individual cleaner or contact
generalizing one account's outcome into a claimed pattern without repeats

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a repeat root cause across two or more accounts, or a routed finding that produced no method change by the next cycle

pros.claim: Comparable post-mortems turn scattered losses into a pattern the broker can act on, usually revealing that a single building class or crew was behind several of them
pros.example: three cancellations in a year all tracing back to sites bid on the same optimistic assumption about restroom fixture load, which is a bid-method fix rather than a retention one

cons.claim: Post-mortems are held under the emotional weight of a loss and drift toward blaming the crew or the client, which produces confident wrong lessons
cons.example: recording 'the client was impossible' for an account whose real first signal was a scope addition logged nine months earlier and never billed

failure_modes: reviewing only losses and never saves, so the moves that actually worked are never identified
holding the review months later when only the final argument is remembered
filing findings without routing them, so the same mistake is re-sold next quarter
acceptance_tests: every cancellation, save and broker-initiated exit in the period has a review recording the first warning signal with its date, the unit that should have caught it, a root-cause attribution, the save cost, and where each finding was routed
each routed finding names a specific change to a method rather than a general resolution
revisit_triggers: a second loss shares a root cause with an earlier one
a routed finding has produced no change by the next review cycle

nodes.definition: Step above the single contract and read the book, because decisions that are right per account can be wrong for the business. Five readings matter. Spread distribution: whether a handful of contracts carry the rest, which makes the book fragile to one loss. Client and buyer concentration: several sites under one client, one property-management company or one regional buyer means a single relationship failure removes multiple contracts at once, and expansion inside a big account deepens exactly this exposure. Route and territory density: accounts clustered geographically are cheaper to supervise, faster to reach for a callback, and far easier to re-crew than an isolated site an hour away, which is why a thin-margin building that anchors a dense route can be worth more than its own spread suggests. Crew concentration: one crew holding several accounts is a single point of failure whose collapse is a multi-account emergency rather than one site's problem. And the broker's own supervisory capacity, which is the real cap on the book - the number of accounts that can be inspected, reviewed and complaint-handled well, beyond which every additional contract degrades the ones already held. The book view is what decides where investment goes: which accounts get expansion effort, which get a re-crew rather than an exit, which low-spread site is kept because it anchors a route or a client, and when the honest answer is to stop selling until supervision catches up.

included: spread distribution, client and buyer concentration, route density, crew concentration and supervisory capacity
using the book view to allocate investment and to defer or confirm exits
the decision to pause selling when capacity is exceeded
excluded: choosing which markets or facility classes to pursue, owned by the acquisition knowledge base
recruiting additional crews or supervisors, owned by the crew sourcing knowledge base
any valuation of the book or claim about what it would sell for

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an account won, lost or exited, a crew taking on or leaving multiple sites, or a change in supervisory capacity or review-cadence adherence

pros.claim: The book view catches the risks no single account shows, especially the moment when adding contracts starts degrading the ones already held
pros.example: recognizing that one crew now covers a cluster of accounts, so its loss would be a multi-site emergency rather than one building's problem

cons.claim: Book-level reasoning can be used to justify keeping a losing contract indefinitely under the label of strategic anchoring
cons.example: an under-water site retained for two years as a route anchor while its complaint load consumed the supervision the neighbouring accounts needed

failure_modes: growing the book past the supervision capacity that the retention engine depends on
letting client or crew concentration build unnoticed because every individual account looks healthy
reading route density as a reason to accept any nearby work regardless of its own spread
acceptance_tests: the book view records spread distribution, the largest client and crew concentrations, route clusters, and the broker's current supervisory capacity against the number of live accounts
any contract retained on book-level grounds despite an under-water band carries a dated remedy plan and a review date
revisit_triggers: an account is won, lost or exited, changing concentration or route density
a crew takes on or gives up multiple sites
supervisory capacity changes, or the promised review cadence starts slipping

edges.why_related: the ledger captures exactly the cost lines the frame declares to be delivered cost for a contract-month
the frame states that the broker's income comes from arranging service others perform, which is the fact the standing disclosure keeps visible to the client
drift can only be attributed to a mechanism when the ledger has recorded the cost lines and their causes month by month
creep is costed in crew hours that must land against the same site and month as every other delivered cost
the read names a dominant mechanism, and cost drift supplies one of the named candidates with its evidence
logged additions with estimated hours are the second named mechanism the variance decomposition draws on
a cause class can only be assigned to a complaint that was captured as an observed fact with site, area, task and service date
the correction vehicle and who bears its cost are determined by the cause class assigned before dispatch
the load trend is computed from closed loops, their closure times and their re-open share, which only the loop produces
the scorecard's money reading is the band and dominant mechanism the margin read assigns
the scorecard's churn-risk reading is the normalized complaint trend, re-open share and reporting altitude
the scorecard's relationship reading is the current state of signer, day-to-day contact and sponsor
the calendar's lead-time alarms are sized and prioritized by the account state the scorecard reports
the case is built to a specific window - term end, escalator anniversary or budget cycle - that only the calendar knows
the conversation presents the assembled evidence and costed options and cannot be held responsibly without them
expansion is offered only to accounts whose combined state is healthy, which is the scorecard's output
the change order disposes of the specific logged addition, with its date, requester and estimated hours
the exit ladder starts from the account's combined state, since unprofitable-and-unhappy and unprofitable-but-liked take different paths
every exit, like every cancellation and save, feeds the fixed post-mortem question set
the book view aggregates per-account states into spread distribution, concentration and capacity readings
the boundary removes the levers that are most tempting precisely in a price meeting - fear framing, manufactured urgency, threatened service decay, and approaching a signer without authority
edges.risk_of_conflict: a broker under cash pressure reaches for a refused lever and wins the renewal at the cost of the relationship's honesty

edges.why_related: expansion offers must not be bundled with price pressure, pushed during an open complaint, or aimed at a signer who cannot properly evaluate them
what the broker promises a complainant must stay inside what the arrangement actually permits it to do, rather than implying direct command over people it does not employ

an obligation-class flag that cannot be satisfied - a lapsed certificate the client requires, a compliance overlay no available crew can meet - can force the exit path regardless of the account's margin
every free re-clean, special dispatch and credit that protects retention is a delivered cost that erodes the same month's spread
edges.resolution_rule: correction is unconditional and free when the cause class is execution or coverage failure; when the class is scope gap or expectation drift, correct once as a recorded goodwill item and convert the recurrence to a change order - response speed and written closure are never the things cut to protect margin

edges.why_related: billing every small addition protects the spread but can cool the day-to-day relationship with the contact who keeps asking for favours
edges.resolution_rule: small additions may be absorbed as recorded goodwill items with an expiry date and are never refused by the cleaner at the moment of the ask; anything recurring, or beyond the recorded goodwill allowance, is raised by the broker at the next review and converted into a change order

edges.why_related: asking for more money and offering more services in the same meeting turns an honest offer into a lever and makes both look like pressure
edges.resolution_rule: never bundle: when both are due, run the repricing to a decision first and raise expansion at a later review, unless the client themselves introduces the expansion, in which case it is priced by the same delivered-cost mechanism and recorded as client-initiated

edges.why_related: the per-contract ladder says exit while the book says the site anchors a dense route, keeps a crew fed, or holds a multi-site client relationship
edges.resolution_rule: book-level anchoring may defer an exit only with a written dated remedy plan and a review date, and never when complaint load makes the site unservable or an obligation-class flag is unresolved; a deferral that passes its review date without improvement converts to exit

edges.why_related: knowing a client's notice window before they do is a commercial advantage that silence would convert into a locked renewal
edges.resolution_rule: the calendar is used to act early on the broker's own side and to inform the client in writing of any window affecting them before it closes; a renewal that depends on the client not knowing their own notice date is refused even when the ledger says the account is worth keeping

edges.why_related: a crew absorbing unpaid extra work, a squeezed rate or repeated turnover shows up weeks later as missed tasks and rising complaints at the same site
unbilled additions stretch the same paid hours across more work, so something in the original scope quietly gets dropped and generates the next complaint
a well-closed complaint is one of the most common origins of expansion, because the client has just seen the broker's accountability demonstrated rather than described
the roles and their states must be current before a review is scheduled, because who attends and how urgent it is depend on who now holds the account
the evidence-based review precedes the price case so that the service record exists and cost pressure has been signalled before any number is presented
an executed change order rewrites the site's price and cost model, so the next margin read compares against the building as it now is rather than as it was bid
post-mortem findings about missed early signals retune the intake channels, severity rules and acknowledgement windows that failed to surface them
supervisory capacity at book level caps the review cadence that can actually be delivered, so promised cadences are reset from the book view rather than from ambition

both are variance-attribution disciplines: an observed symptom is assigned to exactly one named mechanism before any remedy is chosen, and both fail the same way when the easiest explanation is accepted

conflict_axes.name: retention_spend_vs_spread_protection
conflict_axes.description: Every free correction, special dispatch and credit that keeps a client also consumes the month's spread, and a retention engine nobody costs will quietly eat the margin it exists to protect.
poles: correct everything free and fast to keep the client
protect the spread and bill what was never sold
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: let the cause class decide who pays - free for execution and coverage failures, a recorded goodwill item once for scope gap and expectation drift, then a change order - and always post the correction cost to the ledger

conflict_axes.name: goodwill_absorption_vs_change_order_discipline
conflict_axes.description: Absorbing small requests keeps the day-to-day contact warm, but unrecorded absorption is the main route by which a correctly priced contract becomes unprofitable without any visible decision.
poles: absorb small asks to protect the relationship
convert every addition into a priced change
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: absorb only inside a recorded allowance with an expiry date, never refuse at the moment of the ask through the cleaner, and raise the accumulated pattern at the next review

conflict_axes.name: crew_cost_pressure_vs_delivered_quality
conflict_axes.description: The fastest way to restore a month's spread is to squeeze what the crew is paid or expect more work for the same money, and the slowest-arriving consequence is the quality collapse that follows.
poles: hold delivered cost down at the crew
pay enough to hold the standard and reprice the client
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: treat a squeeze as a deferred complaint: name the drift mechanism first, and if the cost is real, take it to the client as a repricing case or restructure the delivery pattern rather than to the crew as a cut

conflict_axes.name: early_disclosure_vs_commercial_advantage
conflict_axes.description: The broker usually knows the client's notice window, escalator and cost pressure before the client does, and every one of those facts is worth more commercially if it is disclosed late.
poles: tell the client early and in plain language
hold the information until it is most useful
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: disclosure of anything that affects the client's own options is not optional or timed for advantage; commercial preparation happens on the broker's side of the calendar, not in the client's ignorance

conflict_axes.name: rescue_effort_vs_exit_discipline
conflict_axes.description: A losing contract can almost always be improved with enough attention, and attention is the broker's scarcest input, so rescue and exit compete for the same hours that healthy accounts also need.
poles: fix the account, cancelling is failure
release it and spend the attention where it pays
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: climb the remedy ladder with deadlines and owners rather than indefinitely; when a rung's deadline passes without result, the ladder advances rather than restarting

conflict_axes.name: per_contract_optimum_vs_book_level_optimum
conflict_axes.description: A contract can be worth keeping for what it does for the book - anchoring a route, feeding a crew, holding a multi-site client - while its own spread says release it.
poles: judge each contract on its own realized spread
judge it by its contribution to the book
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: book value may buy a dated remedy plan, never permanent tolerance; the anchoring claim must be written down with the route, crew or client it protects and reviewed on a date

conflict_axes.name: expansion_growth_vs_supervision_capacity
conflict_axes.description: Added frequency, periodic services and sister sites are the cheapest revenue available, and each one consumes the inspection, review and complaint-handling attention that keeps the existing accounts healthy.
poles: take the growth while the relationship is warm
protect the capacity the retention engine runs on
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: gate every expansion offer on a crew capacity and capability check and on the broker's own remaining supervisory headroom, and pause offers when the promised review cadence is already slipping

conflict_axes.name: response_speed_vs_correct_diagnosis
conflict_axes.description: Clients judge the broker on how fast a human responds, while dispatching before the cause is classified is how out-of-scope work becomes a permanent free obligation.
poles: dispatch immediately, argue later
classify the cause before anyone is sent
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: separate the clocks: acknowledge fast and unconditionally, then classify before choosing the correction vehicle, and let severity - not the client's tone - decide whether a special dispatch is warranted

conflict_axes.name: tighter_crew_direction_vs_classification_risk_class
conflict_axes.description: The obvious operational answer to a quality problem is for the broker to direct the crew's people, schedules and methods more closely, which moves the arrangement toward the control signals that sit at the centre of the worker-classification risk class.
poles: direct the work more tightly to fix quality
keep the arrangement as engaged and route the question
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: route any remedy that increases direction or control to the compliance watch and a qualified professional in the relevant jurisdiction before adopting it; prefer remedies that change the specification, the inspection or the crew rather than the degree of control

conflict_axes.name: comfortable_blame_vs_honest_attribution_after_a_loss
conflict_axes.description: When an account is lost or an account-month goes under water, the cheapest explanations available are the crew and the client, while the honest attribution is often the bid's own assumptions, an addition nobody billed, or attention the broker never gave the account.
poles: accept the explanation that is easiest to say out loud
attribute to the mechanism the records actually support
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: require the attribution to point at a dated record - a ledger line, a logged addition, a complaint closure time, a missed review - before it is accepted, and route findings that implicate the bid method or the broker's own capacity outward rather than absorbing them as crew failure

edge_cases.description: A quarterly floor refinish and an annual carpet extraction both land in one month and make a healthy account read as collapsed
edge_cases.trigger: periodic project work concentrates its cost and billing into a single read
edge_cases.mitigation: smooth periodic work across the term before assigning a band, mark project months as unreliable for band changes, and require two consecutive reads before any remedy is triggered

edge_cases.description: The facility manager who selected the broker leaves and the successor arrives with a preferred vendor and a mandate to cut costs
edge_cases.trigger: sponsor turnover at a client mid-term
edge_cases.mitigation: treat as a same-week priority: re-introduce the service model, re-walk the scope, agree in writing what good looks like at this site, bring the review forward with the closure and inspection record, and check the notice window before assuming there is time

edge_cases.description: The client asks to hire the crew directly, or the crew approaches the client behind the broker
edge_cases.trigger: either party proposes removing the broker from the arrangement
edge_cases.mitigation: answer honestly about the model and state the broker's actual value - coverage, supervision, backup, one invoice and one accountable party; route any non-solicitation clause question to a qualified professional rather than asserting its effect; then decide on the merits whether to reprice, restructure or transition, never to misrepresent

edge_cases.description: A client withholds payment over a quality dispute while the crew must still be paid for work already performed this month
edge_cases.trigger: a disputed invoice collides with the crew's payment cycle
edge_cases.mitigation: separate the two disputes: close the quality complaints through the loop with verification evidence, keep the crew paid for work performed so the site does not degrade mid-dispute, record the withheld amount and its cause in the ledger, and treat repeated withholding as an exit trigger rather than a negotiating style to absorb

edge_cases.description: A recurring complaint turns out to be a task that was never in the contract and has been re-cleaned free for months
edge_cases.trigger: root-cause classification reveals a scope gap behind a familiar complaint
edge_cases.mitigation: stop the silent absorption with a dated decision: either a change order that prices the task from an effective date or a recorded goodwill item with an expiry, explained to the client as a clarification of what was purchased rather than as a withdrawal of service

edge_cases.description: An insurance certificate, bond or added-insured endorsement lapses mid-term and the client's contract requires it
edge_cases.trigger: a certificate expiry or endorsement change passes unnoticed
edge_cases.mitigation: hold expiry dates in the calendar with lead-time alarms, freeze affected decisions when a flag opens, and route the question of what the lapse means for service continuity and liability to a qualified professional rather than deciding it operationally

edge_cases.description: The building's use changes materially with no scope change - occupancy doubles, a tenant adds food service or a gym, or a hybrid schedule empties three floors
edge_cases.trigger: client-side change in occupancy, tenancy or hours
edge_cases.mitigation: classify the resulting complaints as expectation drift, re-measure what the work has become, and run the case in whichever direction the evidence points - including a price reduction where the work genuinely fell, which is the strongest credibility the broker can hold for the increase it will one day need

edge_cases.description: An auto-renew fires unnoticed and locks a full term at a price the ledger already showed as losing
edge_cases.trigger: a notice window passes without an alarm or a decision
edge_cases.mitigation: audit the calendar's coverage against the contract files, and where a term has already locked, seek an honest mid-term change order supported by the evidence pack rather than degrading service or seeking a technicality to escape

edge_cases.description: A single crew that holds several of the broker's accounts quits, is lost to a competitor, or fails all at once
edge_cases.trigger: crew concentration failure across multiple sites
edge_cases.mitigation: watch crew concentration at book level before it happens; when it does, tell every affected client early and honestly rather than letting them discover strangers in their building, and expect the complaint load at every affected site to rise through the transition (the backup coverage design itself belongs to the crew sourcing knowledge base)

edge_cases.description: A property-management company takes over the building, or the client centralizes purchasing at a regional office, and every service contract goes out to bid as routine policy
edge_cases.trigger: the buying entity changes above the day-to-day contact
edge_cases.mitigation: meet the new buyer early with the service record rather than waiting to be included in a tender, expect a procurement process rather than a relationship decision, and re-read the book's concentration exposure if that buyer controls several of the broker's sites

edge_cases.description: The complainant is an occupant or tenant with no contractual relationship to the broker, emailing directly and asking for changes
edge_cases.trigger: a non-contracting party opens a service channel
edge_cases.mitigation: log and act on the observation like any other, because ignoring it produces an escalation, but route every scope or cost decision back to the contract holder and tell the occupant plainly who the broker's client is, so a second unaccountable scope channel never opens

edge_cases.description: A client demands the same named cleaners permanently, sets their hours directly, and asks the broker to supervise them minute by minute after a quality problem
edge_cases.trigger: client pressure moves the working arrangement toward direct control of specific individuals
edge_cases.mitigation: raise a flag in the register, route the classification question to a qualified professional in the relevant jurisdiction before agreeing, and offer remedies that meet the client's real need - a tighter specification, more inspection, or a different crew - rather than an arrangement change nobody has verified

workflow.action: Fix what each live contract is accountable for
workflow.description: State the contract-month unit, the delivered-cost lines that count, and the three health outcomes an account can sit in
workflow.artifact: post-signature accountability statement covering the book
workflow.gate: the unit, the cost-line list and the three outcomes are written and each live contract is assigned to one of them

workflow.action: Restate the service model to every current client contact
workflow.description: Confirm each account's signer and day-to-day contact know that contracted crews perform the work, who supervises them and who to call
workflow.artifact: dated per-account disclosure record including crew-change notifications
workflow.gate: every account has a dated record showing the current contact was told the model, with no contact inherited silently

workflow.action: Open the per-contract ledger and start capturing every cost line
workflow.description: Record invoiced and collected revenue, every delivered-cost line with its cause, payment behaviour and the broker's own hours, against site and month
workflow.gate: for any live contract and recent month the ledger returns revenue, costed lines with causes and the realized spread without reconstruction from memory

workflow.action: Run the monthly margin read and band every contract
workflow.description: Compare realized spread to the bid model, decompose the gap into named mechanisms, smooth periodic work, assign a band and a corrective owner
workflow.artifact: banded variance sheet with one dominant mechanism per contract
workflow.gate: every contract has a band, a named dominant mechanism, a corrective owner and a consecutive-read count, with project months marked

workflow.action: Install single-channel complaint intake and written severity rules
workflow.description: Funnel every arrival channel into one dated log with observed facts, assign severity, and start the acknowledgement clock
workflow.artifact: one complaint log with severity rules and acknowledgement targets
workflow.gate: every complaint from any channel exists as one dated record with severity assigned, and crew-raised site issues appear in the same log

workflow.action: Classify cause before dispatching, then close every complaint through the loop
workflow.description: Assign one cause class, correct by the severity-appropriate vehicle, verify physically or by dated evidence, close in writing, and post the cost to the ledger
workflow.artifact: closed-complaint records with cause class, verification evidence and correction cost
workflow.gate: no complaint is closed without verification and a written closure message, and each correction's cost appears against the site and month

workflow.action: Map the account's people and set the review cadence
workflow.description: Record signer, day-to-day contact and sponsor with their states, then schedule reviews proportional to value and fragility and placed ahead of renewal windows
workflow.artifact: relationship map plus a scheduled review calendar with evidence packs
workflow.gate: every account names its three roles with a verification date and has a next review scheduled before its notice window opens

workflow.action: Score every account and build the ranked action queue
workflow.description: Combine margin band, complaint trend, relationship state, runway and payment behaviour into one state per account with an owner and a next step
workflow.artifact: ranked account action queue refreshed on the margin-read cadence
workflow.gate: every live account carries the four readings, one owner and one next step, and top items show dated action since the last refresh

workflow.action: Load the renewal, notice, escalator and certificate calendar
workflow.description: Enter term ends, auto-renew triggers, notice periods, escalator dates, certificate expiries and client budget cycles with lead-time alarms
workflow.artifact: operating calendar with lead-time alarms and referral notes
workflow.gate: every account's dates are entered with alarms long enough to act, and clause-interpretation questions are recorded as professional referrals rather than rulings

workflow.action: Dispose of every logged scope addition through a change order or a recorded goodwill item
workflow.description: Update the client's price, the crew's scope and pay, and the ledger's cost model together from one effective date with an authorized approver
workflow.artifact: signed change orders and dated goodwill items with expiries
workflow.gate: no logged addition remains undisposed at the next read, and every change order shows matching price, crew-scope and ledger updates with a named authorized approver

workflow.action: Build the repricing case and run the conversation where the read demands it
workflow.description: Assemble dated cost drivers, logged additions, the service record and building changes into at least two costed options, then hold the conversation early with the decision-maker
workflow.artifact: repricing evidence pack with costed options and a recorded walk-away spread
workflow.gate: each option carries its own delivered-cost model and a staffing check, and the walk-away spread is recorded before the meeting is held

workflow.action: Decide expand, hold, remedy or exit for each account, and post-mortem every outcome
workflow.description: Climb the remedy ladder with deadlines and owners, exit only on a named trigger, and review every cancellation, save and exit against the fixed question set
workflow.artifact: per-account decision record with remedy ladder history, exit duties checklist and routed post-mortem findings
workflow.gate: no exit occurs without the ladder attempted and dated, notice honored, the client informed first, crew given notice and access credentials returned against a signed record

priority_rationale: The frame, the disclosure duty, the ethical boundary and the obligation-class watch come first because every later move is judged against them and because a retention or repricing action taken outside them cannot be undone. Measurement follows: the ledger, then the two cost mechanisms that explain it, then the margin read that turns them into a banded diagnosis, because no remedy is trustworthy before the variance is attributed. The complaint chain - intake, cause classification, the closure loop, and load as a signal - sits next because it is simultaneously the retention engine and a cost mechanism visible in the same ledger. The relationship map, review cadence and scorecard compose money, quality and people into one account state, which is what makes the commercial units possible: the calendar that sets timing, the change-order discipline that stops creep re-entering, the case and the conversation that reprice honestly, and the expansion ladder that only healthy accounts qualify for. The exit ladder, the post-mortem and the book-level view come last because each consumes the outputs of everything above it and feeds the acquisition and crew methods that sit outside this knowledge base.

dominance_rules.rule: Honest disclosure of the service model dominates any retention, repricing or expansion tactic
dominance_rules.rationale: the client will eventually meet the crew, and a relationship built on a misunderstanding of who cleans the building cannot be repaired by service recovery
dominance_rules.trigger: any client communication where the arrangement could be blurred, including complaint responses and crew changes
dominance_rules.action: state the arrangement plainly, even where doing so invites the disintermediation question or costs the account

dominance_rules.rationale: classification, insurance, bonding, non-solicitation and termination questions vary by jurisdiction and year, and an in-house guess creates exposure that no month's margin justifies
dominance_rules.trigger: a live-account fact touches a classification, insurance, bonding, compliance or clause-enforceability question
dominance_rules.action: freeze the affected decision, log it in the flag register, and route it to a qualified professional before acting

dominance_rules.rule: Safety, biohazard and security failures dominate the triage queue and the margin calculus
dominance_rules.rationale: these failures carry consequences for people and for the client's own obligations that no cost comparison can offset
dominance_rules.trigger: a complaint or crew report involving safety, biohazard exposure, or a building left unsecured
dominance_rules.action: handle the same day regardless of cost, then classify cause and recover the commercial position afterwards

dominance_rules.rule: Ledger evidence dominates recollection in any margin dispute
dominance_rules.rationale: a remedy aimed at a mechanism nobody measured usually lands on the crew, who are the easiest party to squeeze and the most expensive to lose
dominance_rules.trigger: someone asserts an account is losing money, or that a cost rose, without ledger lines showing it
dominance_rules.action: return the claim to measurement before it reaches the crew or the client

dominance_rules.rule: The complaint's cause class dominates who pays for the correction
dominance_rules.rationale: charging a client for the broker's own execution failure destroys trust, and re-cleaning free forever what was never sold destroys the spread
dominance_rules.trigger: a correction is about to be dispatched or invoiced
dominance_rules.action: assign exactly one cause class first and apply its routing rule, free for execution and coverage failures, commercial for scope gap and expectation drift

dominance_rules.rule: Written closure to the complainant dominates the speed of the physical correction
dominance_rules.rationale: clients forgive misses and cancel over silence; an unreported fix is remembered only as the original problem
dominance_rules.trigger: a correction has been completed and verified but the complainant has not been told
dominance_rules.action: close in writing with what was found, what was corrected and what changed, before the item leaves the queue

dominance_rules.rule: The pre-set walk-away spread dominates any concession made inside a meeting
dominance_rules.rationale: the fear of losing an account is at its peak in the room, which is precisely where a permanent concession should not be decided
dominance_rules.trigger: a client pushes for terms below the spread recorded before the conversation
dominance_rules.action: leave the meeting with the option open and re-decide in writing outside it, or hold at the floor and offer the scope-reduction option

dominance_rules.rule: The client's own notice and renewal rights dominate the broker's calendar advantage
dominance_rules.rationale: a renewal obtained through the client's forgetfulness is the lever this method refuses, and it converts one saved account into a reputation the referral base will not survive
dominance_rules.trigger: a notice window, auto-renew trigger or escalator date approaches
dominance_rules.action: inform the client in writing while they can still act, and prepare the broker's own case in parallel

dominance_rules.rule: When per-contract exit logic and book-level anchoring disagree, the ladder advances unless a dated remedy plan exists
dominance_rules.rationale: route density and crew feeding are real benefits, but 'strategic' is the most common label for a loss nobody wants to face
dominance_rules.trigger: an under-water account is proposed for retention on book-level grounds
dominance_rules.action: require a written remedy plan naming the route, crew or client it protects and a review date; convert to exit if the date passes without improvement, and exit regardless when the site is unservable or a flag is unresolved

anti_rework_rules.rule: Open the ledger and capture cost lines before diagnosing any account's margin
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a diagnosis built from memory that aims the remedy at the crew when the mechanism was scope creep, forcing a second diagnosis after the crew has already been damaged

anti_rework_rules.rule: Classify a complaint's cause class before dispatching a correction
anti_rework_rules.prevents: free re-cleans that convert an out-of-scope task into a permanent obligation the next renewal has to price around

anti_rework_rules.rule: Log scope additions on the day they are requested, with requester and estimated hours
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a repricing case built on unprovable claims that the client's own contact reasonably denies, collapsing the credibility of the whole pack

anti_rework_rules.rule: Update client price, crew scope and pay, and the ledger cost model in the same change order
anti_rework_rules.prevents: crews doing unbilled work until they resign the site, or clients paying more for work that visibly never changed

anti_rework_rules.rule: Re-onboard a new client contact before their first complaint, not after it
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a rebid triggered by a stranger who judged the account on one bad night with none of the history that earned the contract

anti_rework_rules.rule: Smooth periodic project work across the term before changing a band
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-crewing or repricing a healthy account on the strength of a single project month, and the relationship damage that follows an unjustified price conversation

anti_rework_rules.rule: Hold an evidence-based service review before any price conversation
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a price case that arrives with no service record, reads as opportunism, and sends the contract straight to tender

anti_rework_rules.rule: Record the walk-away spread before entering a repricing meeting
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a concession made under pressure that must later be unwound with the same client, or an exit that costs more than holding the account would have

anti_rework_rules.rule: Check crew capacity and capability before offering an expansion
anti_rework_rules.prevents: converting a clean account into a complaint generator and spending the next quarter rescuing what was sold in ten minutes

anti_rework_rules.rule: Enter term, notice, escalator and certificate dates when the contract is signed, not when it is expiring
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a locked term at a losing price and the ugly mid-term renegotiation or service decay that tends to follow it

iteration_protocol.trigger: a contract's band sits at eroding or under water for two consecutive reads
iteration_protocol.action: name the dominant mechanism, open a remedy with a deadline and an owner, and re-read before the next cycle rather than waiting for renewal

iteration_protocol.trigger: a closed complaint re-opens, or a site's normalized complaint load rises for two consecutive reads
iteration_protocol.action: re-run root-cause classification across that site's recent complaints, look for area or task concentration, and escalate to a crew decision or a scope decision instead of another correction

iteration_protocol.trigger: a signer, day-to-day contact or sponsor changes, or the building changes ownership or management company
iteration_protocol.action: re-onboard within the week - restate the service model, re-walk the scope, agree what good looks like in writing - and bring the next service review forward with the evidence pack

iteration_protocol.trigger: a live-account fact touches an obligation class - drift toward control over a crew, an expiring certificate or endorsement, a new site compliance requirement, or a contested clause
iteration_protocol.action: freeze the affected decision, log the flag with its trigger date and owner, and route it to a qualified professional in the relevant jurisdiction before proceeding

iteration_protocol.trigger: a renewal, notice, escalator or certificate alarm fires on the calendar
iteration_protocol.action: run the service review, refresh the margin read and the scorecard, and decide renew, reprice, restructure or exit before the window closes

iteration_protocol.trigger: a crew renegotiates, is replaced, or reports a change in the hours a site actually takes
iteration_protocol.action: re-cost the site from the ledger, attribute the change to a named drift mechanism, and test whether the spread survives before agreeing to anything

iteration_protocol.trigger: an account cancels, is saved after a cancellation threat, or is exited by the broker
iteration_protocol.action: hold the fixed-question post-mortem within weeks and route each finding to the bid method, the crew method, or to a concrete change in this one

iteration_protocol.trigger: client concentration, crew concentration or supervisory load crosses the limit the book view records, or the promised review cadence starts slipping
iteration_protocol.action: pause expansion offers, rebalance attention toward the exposed cluster, and treat added supervision capacity as the precondition for further growth
